ai.description: The Koyna Toad reaches 30–40 mm. It is dark brown with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe and granular skin. A prominent, rounded snout and lack of cranial crests distinguish this species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Koyna Toad is best distinguished by its unique, prominent, and distinctively pointed snout, which is significantly more elongated than that of other Indian toad species.
ai.habitat: The Koyna Toad inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and grasslands in the Northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Koyna toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging from rock crevices during the monsoon season to forage for small invertebrates in the moist forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Koyna toad is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in seasonal rock pools. It breeds during the monsoon season, typically producing small clutches of aquatic eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Koyna Toad (*Beduka koynayensis*) is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation areas around the Koyna region.
ai.callDescription: The Koyna Toad’s advertisement call is a series of pulsed, high-pitched metallic chirps, typically heard emanating from rocky stream beds during the monsoon season.
